subject: Citizen input for CC meeting 05/04/23
comment:
I see no advantage for St. George citizens with this e-bus proposal. The following are my concerns regarding electric vehicles (EVs) and the push to electrify everything:

1. EVs are heavily subsidized by taxpayers and would not be viable in the marketplace without those subsidies.
2. The electric grid is already strained and cannot reliably support large-scale EV adoption, especially in the heat of southern Utah summers.
3. The batteries require mining of rare-earth minerals, much of it done overseas under poor environmental and labor conditions.
4. EV batteries are expensive to replace and difficult to recycle, creating a future disposal problem.
5. The range of electric buses is limited, and performance degrades in extreme temperatures.
6. The up-front and maintenance costs of electric buses exceed those of conventional vehicles.
7. The claimed climate/emissions benefits are overstated once the full life cycle (manufacturing, electricity generation, disposal) is considered.
8. Charging infrastructure is costly and would be funded by taxpayers.
9. This is a top-down agenda being pushed onto the city that does not reflect the actual needs or wishes of St. George citizens.

Please rethink any use of Electric vehicles, appliances, landscaping tools, etc. in the city. Thank you.

subject: Opposition to Zion shuttle service proposal
comment:
Good Evening Mayor Randall, and City Council Members:

My Question is, what is the benefit for the tax payer in St. George?

My second question is, who makes money from this shuttle service?

The hotels are almost always filled with visitors, how would our city benefit?

We have tourism without a shuttle bus to Zion. I would suggest that the city reject this shuttle service!

Thank You

Curt Sorweid, St. George, 84790

subject: PUBLIC COMMENTS
comment:
To St. George City Officials:

I am Donna Williams and I also speak for my husband Ernest Phildon Williams; address: St. George.

Since no public comments were allowed last night, please include these comments in your record and minutes of your May 4th meeting:

(1) The City of St. George should absolutely be accepting and welcoming public comment on all issues if we are still a Constitutional Republic (which you say you are in your Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States of America.) By cancelling the voices you may not want to hear, you are cancelling Freedom of Speech of which we are guaranteed in our First Amendment. (Item #2 on your Agenda.)

(2) The shuttle proposal should not have been voted on with other issues; but should have received a separate up and down vote. And it should be known that such an endeavor, though it may sound like a nice idea; is not part of City Government, as it competes with other transportation businesses already operating on a free market basis. Government has no place competing with private businesses. Tourism is a tricky subject; but we don't need incentives to bring it here, it's obvious with all the restrictions at Zion Park that such is the case. (Item #3 on your Agenda.)

(3) Our City is the Board of Canvassers for the upcoming elections; and as such is authorized to implement hand-counted ballots in municipal primary elections this year. This will restore public trust in the process, eliminating current vulnerabilities to software errors and digital manipulation. (Miscellaneous Item not on Agenda.)

Respectfully,
Donna and Ernest Phildon Williams

subject: Public Comment on Restoring Trust
comment: Southern Utahns for Transparency submits this public comment regarding restoring trust in our elections and improving public comment policy. We ask that Washington County and city officials return to hand-counting ballots beginning with the 2023 municipal primary elections to restore public trust by eliminating vulnerabilities to software errors and/or digital manipulation; that the county begin voter canvassing and Cast Vote Record analysis with the help of an independent professional statistician as a further check against ballot-stuffing; that public comment policy be improved to align with Class 1 and 2 counties in Utah (open public comment without signup, at least 3 minutes each for unlimited persons, especially before any voting or election certification); and that the county and city websites be improved with a single grid that includes links to all minutes, recordings, and advance agendas so the public is informed ahead of time. Attached are our petition materials and signature lists.

subject: Public Comment
comment:
I was shocked when the declaration of NO public comments at the first council meeting of the month was announced. Public comment is a vital part of representative government and should not be eliminated or curtailed. I propose the following rules for a public comment policy:

1. Public comment should be allowed at every regular council meeting.
2. No advance sign-up should be required to speak.
3. Each speaker should be allowed at least three minutes.
4. Comments should be allowed before any vote is taken on an agenda item.
5. The council should not limit the number of speakers.
6. Speakers should be treated with respect and not interrupted.
7. The council should respond to or follow up on substantive concerns raised.
8. The policy should be published and applied consistently.

Thank you for considering these suggestions.

Rich F

subject: Fwd: Public comments
comment:
Dear Mrs. Mayor,

Yes, you will get the same people coming to public comment meeting after meeting, but that is their right as citizens. Eliminating or restricting public comment is not the answer. Public comment is one of the few ways ordinary citizens can be heard by their elected officials, and it should be preserved and protected, not curtailed for the convenience of the council. Please reconsider any policy that limits the public's ability to speak.

Thank you.
